TradeWatch

Trade intelligence infrastructure for a contested world.

Customs clearance · automated Marine insurance evidence · reviewed Letter of Credit · document-ready

Global trade
is getting increasingly complex.

Every shipment requires synchronized customs clearance, cargo insurance, and trade finance to mitigate regulatory and financial risks.

01 · Customs

The Customs Authority

Decides if your shipment can leave the country

What they check
Permission to exportActive export licence
Product categoryCorrectly classified
Declared valueMatches your invoice
Supporting documentsInvoice, packing list, transport docs

Does not see what Insurance or the Bank checks.

Get one detail wrong and your shipment can sit at the port for days, sometimes weeks — after the container is already there.

02 · Insurance

The Insurance Provider

Pays out if something happens in transit

What they check
Cover amountBig enough for the cargo
What's being shippedDeclared correctly
Route and methodCovered by the policy
The person insuringActually owns the cargo

Does not see what Customs or the Bank checks.

If the policy says one thing and your shipment is another, the insurer denies the claim — when you need it most.

03 · Payment

The Trade Finance Bank

Releases your payment once documents are perfect

What they check
Who gets paidMatches the contract
AmountMatches every document
Documents presentAll required papers in
Every number agreesAcross every document

Does not see what Customs or Insurance checks.

A USD 150 difference between your invoice and packing list is enough to delay payment by weeks.

A single shipment touches multiple decision surfaces.

What exporters need is not another dashboard to manage.

The Kanan Roadmap

From shipment evidence
to persistent trade intelligence.

TradeWatch starts with the documents that decide whether a shipment can move, be insured, or be defended later. The same evidence layer compounds into broader trade-risk intelligence over time.

Now

TradeWatch

PoC · EV-Component Exports

Reviewed evidence packets for customs and marine cargo insurance handoff.

Exporters share the shipment bundle. TradeWatch reconciles the documents, checks the applicable evidence requirements, flags gaps, and prepares two reviewed packets before the CHA or insurance broker has to reject, query, or correct them.

EndpointsCHA handoff · Insurance broker handoff
ScopeEV-component export shipments
OutputReviewed packet · discrepancy report · evidence trail

Evidence Layer

MVP Expansion · Multi-Surface

One shipment fact model projected into multiple institutional surfaces.

Drona · the engine inside TradeWatch

Software waits to be asked.
TradeWatch is already watching your file.

Most trade tools sit idle until you log in. We've codified what a senior trade consultant actually does — read every notification, cross-check every document, test it against your own policy — and put it to work continuously.

Most trade tools sit idle until you log in. We codified what a senior trade consultant actually does, and put it to work continuously.

Drona is the neurosymbolic engine that makes that possible

01 · Input

What we read

Customs notifications & circulars Quality control orders Foreign regulations & sanctions lists Customs rulings & tribunal decisions Industry standards Insurance & banking circulars

Every source kept, dated, and traceable. Nothing summarised away.

02 · Process

What we do with it

ReadsPulls every relevant fact. Classifies it. Marks ambiguity.
ReasonsTests each obligation against the regulation, your shipment, and your own policy framework.
RecordsLocks the evidence, the reasoning chain, and the reviewer's sign-off. The answer can always be defended.

No black box. No chatbot guessing. The answer always has a paper trail.

03 · Output

What comes out

One reviewed packet for your customs broker. One for your insurer. Both projected from the same shipment.
